newsitem.title: USA: US GDP seen at 2.5 pct in Q2, Q3--Phila Fed survey.
newsitem.headline: US GDP seen at 2.5 pct in Q2, Q3--Phila Fed survey.

text.p: The U.S. economy is likely to expand at a 2.5 percent annual rate in the second quarter of 1997, said economists surveyed by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
The 40 economists participating in the Survey of Professional Forecasters projected a growth rate of 2.5 percent for the third quarter and 2.3 percent for the fourth quarter.
Economists surveyed said they expected average GDP growth of 3.6 percent in 1997.
The survey showed the U.S. Consumer Price Index is likely to rise by 2.5 percent in the second quarter followed by an increase of 2.8 percent in the third and up 3.0 percent in the fourth quarter.
Overall, consumer prices are seen up 2.7 percent in 1997.
The three-month Treasury bill rate is expected to stand, on average, at 5.3 percent in the second quarter and at 5.5 percent in the third.
Forecasters pegged the three-month T-bill rate at 5.3 percent for all of 1997.
The respondents looked for an unemployment rate of 5.0 percent in the second quarter, 5.1 percent in the third and fourth quarters and 5.1 percent for the average 1997.
